papers.title: Identifying phase separation modulators mediated by the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein using a structure-based drug discovery approach.
papers.abstract: As severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) continues to evolve through mutations and acquire resistance to existing antiviral agents, the persistence of post-pandemic infections remains a significant global health concern. To address these challenges, it is crucial to develop novel therapeutic agents that target previously unexplored viral or host mechanisms.
papers.summary: This study uses a structure-based drug discovery approach to identify small molecules that modulate phase separation driven by the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein, a viral mechanism not targeted by current antivirals. The work aims to find new therapeutic candidates that could remain effective as the virus evolves and acquires resistance to existing drugs.

papers.title: The pharmacological potential and metabolic risks of Xiaojin Pill in sorafenib-resistant papillary thyroid carcinoma: an integrated network analysis.
papers.abstract: Sorafenib resistance limits the efficacy of treatments for advanced papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC). The antitumor potential of Xiaojin Pill (XJP) has been demonstrated, yet its mechanisms potentially implicated in sorafenib resistance and combinational toxicological risks remain unclear. This study aimed to examine the molecular mechanisms through which XJP may act on signaling pathways implicated in sorafenib resistance, and to assess its combinational toxicological risks during co-administration with sorafenib.
papers.summary: This study uses integrated network analysis to predict how the traditional Chinese medicine Xiaojin Pill might act on signaling pathways involved in sorafenib resistance in papillary thyroid carcinoma, and to assess toxicological risks when combined with sorafenib. The work is largely computational and predictive, identifying candidate mechanisms and potential combination safety concerns rather than providing experimental validation.

papers.title: GolgiFold: A Structural Predictome of Human Golgi Protein Complexes.
papers.abstract: The Golgi apparatus is a central hub for protein secretion and endolysosomal biogenesis, coordinating protein and vesicular trafficking pathways that maintain cellular homeostasis. Although hundreds of proteins associate with the Golgi, molecular assemblies have been defined for only a subset. Such well-characterized complexes have provided fundamental insights into Golgi trafficking, protein processing, and homeostasis, suggesting that systematic mapping of the broader Golgi interactome would uncover unrecognized components and regulatory mechanisms. Here, we systematically interrogate Golgi
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: GolgiFold presents a systematic structural predictome of human Golgi protein complexes, using computational structure prediction to map molecular assemblies across the Golgi interactome. The work aims to define complexes for the many Golgi-associated proteins whose assemblies remain uncharacterized, potentially revealing unrecognized components and regulatory mechanisms in Golgi trafficking and homeostasis.

papers.title: Domain-Aware Enzyme Classification via Multiple Instance Learning.
papers.abstract: Accurate Enzyme Commission (EC) number prediction is fundamental to protein function annotation and metabolic pathway reconstruction. Recent methods based on protein language model embeddings or 3D structure have improved EC prediction, but important limitations remain. Whole-sequence embeddings can dilute local functional signals, such as catalytic residues and functional domains, whereas structure-based methods depend on accurate protein structures and are therefore difficult to apply broadly.
papers.summary: The paper introduces a domain-aware enzyme classification method that uses multiple instance learning to focus on local functional regions (e.g., catalytic residues and domains) rather than whole-sequence embeddings, avoiding dependence on accurate 3D structures. This addresses limitations of existing protein language model and structure-based EC number prediction approaches, aiming to improve protein function annotation and metabolic pathway reconstruction.

papers.title: Structural clustering across the tree of life reveals candidate Asgard-eukaryote homologs and a shared expansion of solenoids.
papers.abstract: Asgard archaea are the closest known prokaryotic relatives of eukaryotes, and their genomes encode many eukaryotic signature proteins (ESPs), homologs of proteins associated with eukaryotic cellular complexity. Because deep divergence limits sequence-based homology detection, structure-based searches are increasingly used to expand the ESP repertoire, but they start from individual Asgard proteins rather than the families those proteins belong to. Here we took a complementary, family-level approach, profiling the taxonomic composition of 1.89 million structural clusters from the AFESM database
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study takes a family-level approach to structural clustering across the tree of life, analyzing 1.89 million structural clusters from the AFESM database to profile their taxonomic composition. By starting from protein families rather than individual Asgard proteins, the authors identify candidate Asgard-eukaryote homologs and uncover a shared expansion of solenoid protein folds. The work expands the known repertoire of eukaryotic signature proteins in Asgard archaea and provides a complementary method for deep homology detection.

papers.title: Discovery of benzimidazole-based selective α-glucosidase inhibitors with an uncompetitive mode of action: synthesis, biological assays and computational studies.
papers.abstract: A series of thirteen 1-(benzyloxy)-2-phenyl-1H-benzo[d]imidazole derivatives was designed, synthesized, and evaluated as α-glucosidase inhibitors. Structure-activity relationship analysis revealed that the presence of a chlorine atom at the C-6 position of the benzimidazole core, combined with suitable substituents on the pendant aromatic rings, was associated with relevant α-glucosidase inhibitory activity. Among the series, compounds 6 and 13 emerged as the most potent derivatives showing IC50 values of 32.35 μM and 15.70 μM, respectively, and greater potency than acarbose (IC50 = 139 μM) un
papers.summary: The authors synthesized thirteen benzimidazole derivatives and tested them as α-glucosidase inhibitors, finding that a chlorine at the C-6 position plus appropriate aromatic substituents boosts activity. Compounds 6 and 13 were the most potent (IC50 32.35 and 15.70 μM), outperforming acarbose (139 μM), and compound 13 acts via an uncompetitive inhibition mode. Computational docking and dynamics studies supported the structure-activity relationships.

papers.title: Development of CYP8B1-specific inhibitors for metabolic diseases.
papers.abstract: Changes in bile acids (BAs) balance lead to various metabolic diseases, yet current treatment options targeting these changes remain severely limited. CYP8B1 (cytochrome P450, family 8, subfamily B, polypeptide 1) is a liver-exclusive enzyme that controls the synthesis of 12α-hydroxylated (12α-OH) BAs. Inhibiting CYP8B1 is an attractive therapeutic strategy for attenuating 12α-OH BA levels, remodeling the gut microbiota and thereby ameliorating metabolic diseases. CYP8B1-specific inhibitors are currently lacking due to structural similarities between the active site of CYP8B1 and other CYPs, a
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint reports the development of CYP8B1-specific inhibitors, a liver enzyme that produces 12α-hydroxylated bile acids implicated in metabolic disease. Selectivity is challenging because CYP8B1's active site resembles other cytochrome P450 enzymes, but the authors identify compounds that preferentially inhibit CYP8B1, offering a potential therapeutic route to remodel bile acid pools and gut microbiota in metabolic disorders.

papers.title: Distance-AF Multimer: A Multi-Step Approach for Protein Complex Structure Modeling with User-Defined Distance Constraints.
papers.abstract: The three-dimensional structure of proteins provides essential insight into the molecular mechanisms underlying their function. Many biological activities are mediated through protein interactions, making accurate structural determination of protein complexes important. Despite significant advances in computational protein structure prediction, there are still many cases where protein complexes are not correctly assembled. In particular, there are cases where experimental data, such as distances between residue pairs in interacting proteins are available, yet existing prediction methods fail t
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Distance-AF Multimer is a new computational pipeline that incorporates user-provided distance constraints between residues into protein complex structure prediction. It addresses cases where standard methods like AlphaFold-Multimer fail to assemble complexes correctly despite available experimental distance data. The approach offers a way to leverage sparse experimental restraints to improve complex modeling.

papers.title: Free-Energy and Molecular Dynamics Analysis of Ser195 and Thr195 Rotameric States in Thrombin.
papers.abstract: Ser195 is highly conserved as the catalytic nucleophile in trypsin-like serine proteases, yet the molecular basis for the strong preference for serine over the chemically similar threonine residue remains unclear. Here, we used well-tempered metadynamics and microsecond-long molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to characterize the conformational energetics of S195 and T195 in thrombin. Well-tempered metadynamics revealed distinct rotameric free-energy landscapes in both the apo and the ligand-bound systems. In the apo state, S195 preferentially occupied a lower-angle rotameric state, while T195
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study uses well-tempered metadynamics and microsecond molecular dynamics simulations to compare the conformational energetics of serine versus threonine at position 195 in thrombin. The authors find that S195 and T195 occupy distinct rotameric free-energy landscapes, with S195 preferring a lower-angle rotamer in the apo state, offering a molecular explanation for why serine is strongly conserved over threonine at this catalytic nucleophile position in trypsin-like serine proteases.

papers.title: Edge-Aware Graph Attention Networks for Interpreting Biophysical Mechanisms from Molecular Dynamics Simulations.
papers.abstract: Graph attention networks (GATs) are emerging as powerful aritficial intelligence (AI) tools for learning biomolecular dynamics, yet extracting mechanistic insight from learned attention remains challenging. Here, we present an interpretable AI approach that combines molecular dynamics prediction with mechanistic interpretation through attention-derived communication networks. We develop three edge-aware GAT models - Edge-Conditioned, Edge-Injected, and Edge-Gated - that differ in how edge information is incorporated during message passing. Relative to a standard GAT, our edge-aware models impr
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint introduces three edge-aware graph attention network variants (Edge-Conditioned, Edge-Injected, Edge-Gated) for learning biomolecular dynamics from molecular dynamics simulations, with the goal of extracting mechanistic insight from learned attention. The edge-aware models reportedly improve prediction performance over a standard GAT and allow attention-derived communication networks to be interpreted as biophysical mechanisms. It is a methods contribution aimed at making AI models of MD more interpretable.

papers.title: Structural Basis for Angiotensin II Type I Receptor G Protein-biased Signaling.
papers.abstract: Biased agonism at the angiotensin II type 1 receptor (AT1R) offers a promising strategy for developing safer cardiovascular therapeutics. While β-arrestin-biased agonism has been extensively investigated, G protein-biased signaling remains poorly understood. Here, we report structures of AT1R coupled to G protein and either the endogenous agonist angiotensin II (AngII) or the G protein-biased agonist TRV055. The ligands adopt similar overall poses, with coordinated rearrangements extending from the orthosteric pocket to the intracellular surface. The structures provide a detailed view of a TM7
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint reports cryo-EM structures of the angiotensin II type 1 receptor (AT1R) bound to G protein with either the natural ligand angiotensin II or the G protein-biased agonist TRV055. The two ligands adopt similar poses but trigger coordinated structural rearrangements that propagate from the ligand-binding pocket to the intracellular surface, revealing how biased signaling is encoded. These structures provide a template for designing safer cardiovascular drugs that preferentially activate G protein rather than β-arrestin pathways.

papers.title: AT1R-Selective Negative Allosteric Modulator Targeting the Epitope for Pathogenic Autoantibody Activation.
papers.abstract: A major therapeutic strategy for managing cardiovascular and renal diseases is the use of angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs). These drugs block both pathogenic and physiological signaling by the angiotensin II type 1 receptor (AT1R) by preventing angiotensin II (AngII) binding to orthosteric pocket in transmembrane portion of AT1R. However, in many autoimmune diseases, AT1R activation is chronically driven by pathogenic autoantibody binding to a distinct extracellular surface located allosteric site. Currently, there are no allosteric inhibitors of AT1R available to mechanistically prevent t
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint describes the development of a negative allosteric modulator that selectively targets the extracellular epitope on AT1R where pathogenic autoantibodies bind, rather than the orthosteric AngII pocket used by conventional ARBs. The goal is to block autoantibody-driven AT1R activation in autoimmune cardiovascular and renal disease while sparing physiological AngII signaling. This represents a conceptually new pharmacological approach to AT1R inhibition.

papers.title: A computational-experimental strategy identifies K-7174 against African swine fever.
papers.abstract: African swine fever (ASF), caused by the African swine fever virus (ASFV), poses a catastrophic threat to global swine production due to the absence of effective vaccines or therapeutics. Targeting the virally encoded RNA polymerase (RNAP), which is essential for viral transcription, offers a promising antiviral strategy. Capitalizing on our previously resolved high-resolution structure of ASFV RNAP, we conducted a rigorous structure-based virtual screening of two compound libraries (T001 and LF1000) to identify selective inhibitors. From 100 candidates validated in vitro, nine compounds ident
papers.summary: The authors used the high-resolution structure of the African swine fever virus RNA polymerase to perform structure-based virtual screening of two compound libraries, identifying K-7174 as a selective inhibitor of the viral enzyme. This computational-experimental pipeline provides a starting point for antiviral development against ASF, a disease with no current vaccines or therapeutics.

papers.title: Structure-based prediction reveals FAM105A as an African swine fever virus I215L interactor.
papers.abstract: African swine fever virus (ASFV) causes a fatal hemorrhagic disease in pigs, leading to severe economic losses worldwide. The viral ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme I215L (E2) is critical for ASFV replication and modulation of host antiviral responses. Host deubiquitinating enzymes (DUBs) bind to E2 enzymes to inhibit the transfer of ubiquitin. In this study, we systematically screened 34 swine DUBs using HDOCK docking and AlphaFold3 modeling, identifying FAM105A as the most probable interactor. Co-immunoprecipitation assay validated the interaction between I215L and FAM105A. Structural analyses r
papers.summary: The authors used HDOCK docking and AlphaFold3 modeling to screen 34 swine deubiquitinating enzymes for interaction with the ASFV ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme I215L, identifying FAM105A as the top candidate. Co-immunoprecipitation experimentally confirmed the I215L–FAM105A interaction. This structure-based prediction pipeline nominates a host factor potentially relevant to ASFV replication and antiviral modulation.

papers.title: HelixWings enables AI-driven enzyme engineering for biomimetic cofactor utilization.
papers.abstract: Biomimetic nicotinamide cofactors, such as nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMNH), can substantially reduce synthesis costs compared with natural cofactors like nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADPH). However, natural enzymes generally exhibit poor activity with these alternative cofactors. Existing engineering approaches, including directed evolution and rational design, remain limited by experimental uncertainty or computational complexity. Here, we developed HelixWings, an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven screening platform that integrates conformational dynamics analysis with s
papers.summary: The authors present HelixWings, an AI-driven screening platform that combines conformational dynamics analysis with sequence-based prediction to engineer enzymes that can use cheaper biomimetic cofactors like NMNH instead of NADPH. This addresses the poor activity of natural enzymes with alternative cofactors, offering a faster alternative to directed evolution and rational design.

papers.title: GPCRAgent: an intelligent multi-agent platform integrating knowledge graphs and large language models for GPCR-targeted drug discovery.
papers.abstract: G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) are major therapeutic targets in drug discovery. However, systematic characterization of GPCR functions and ligand interactions remains constrained by the high cost and complexity of experimental approaches. Although large language models (LLMs) have shown strong performance in biomedical question answering, their direct application to GPCR research is limited by insufficient integration of structured domain knowledge and poor interpretability of generated inferences.
papers.summary: GPCRAgent is a multi-agent platform that combines knowledge graphs with large language models to support GPCR-targeted drug discovery. The system aims to overcome LLM limitations in GPCR research—namely weak integration of structured domain knowledge and poor interpretability—by grounding model reasoning in a curated knowledge graph. It offers a systematic, interpretable approach to characterizing GPCR functions and ligand interactions without relying solely on costly experiments.

papers.title: Identification of ebastine and ceritinib as effective inhibitors of Fusobacterium nucleatum FtsZ.
papers.abstract: The role of microorganisms in cancer is not a new concept-bacteria, parasites, and viruses have all been implicated in cancer development. Fusobacterium nucleatum, a member of the oral microbiota, has emerged as an important cancer-associated bacterium. Unbiased global genomic analyses have demonstrated that F. nucleatum is enriched in human colorectal cancer (CRC) tissues compared with noncancerous colorectal tissues, underscoring the urgent need for specific antimicrobial agents targeting F. nucleatum for CRC prevention and treatment. In this study, structure-based virtual screening successf
papers.summary: The authors used structure-based virtual screening to identify two existing drugs, ebastine and ceritinib, as inhibitors of FtsZ, a key bacterial cell-division protein in Fusobacterium nucleatum. Since this oral bacterium is enriched in colorectal cancer tissues, these repurposed drugs could offer a targeted antimicrobial strategy for CRC prevention or treatment.

papers.title: Integrating noncanonical amino acids and synthetic cofactors for the development of artificial metalloenzymes.
papers.abstract: Natural metalloenzymes harness the sophisticated synergy between canonical amino acids and metal cofactors to catalyze life-sustaining reactions. However, the limited chemical diversity of the twenty standard amino acids often restricts non-natural transformations. To overcome these constraints, artificial metalloenzymes (ArMs) integrate synthetic cofactors into protein scaffolds to enable unnatural catalytic functions. This review highlights how noncanonical amino acids (ncAAs) bridge the gap between natural enzyme architecture and synthetic chemistry. We examine genetic code expansion and co
papers.summary: This review discusses how artificial metalloenzymes (ArMs) combine synthetic metal cofactors with protein scaffolds to enable reactions not found in nature. It focuses on noncanonical amino acids (ncAAs) as a bridge between natural enzyme architecture and synthetic chemistry, covering genetic code expansion and cofactor integration strategies. The work surveys the design principles for engineering these hybrid biocatalysts.

papers.title: Bacterial protein function prediction via multimodal deep learning.
papers.abstract: Bacterial proteins are specialized with extensive functional diversity for survival in diverse and stressful environments. A significant portion of these proteins remains functionally uncharacterized, limiting our understanding of bacterial survival mechanisms. Hence, we develop Deep Expression STructure (DeepEST), a multimodal deep learning framework that predicts protein function in bacteria by assigning Gene Ontology (GO) terms. DeepEST comprises two modules: a multi-layer perceptron that uses gene expression and gene location, and a protein structure-based module that uses predicted struct
papers.summary: The authors present DeepEST, a multimodal deep learning framework that predicts Gene Ontology terms for bacterial proteins by combining gene expression, genomic location, and predicted protein structure. This approach addresses the large fraction of bacterial proteins that remain functionally uncharacterized, offering a new tool for annotating function in diverse and stressful environments.

papers.title: The evolutionary conserved protein-RNA interface formed by the cell-fate regulator Bicaudal-C.
papers.abstract: Bicaudal-C (Bicc1) is an essential cell-fate regulator that guides the animal body plan during early development and maintains organ homeostasis in adults. It does so by binding specific mRNA targets and regulating their translation, yet the molecular basis of mRNA target selection has remained unclear. Here, we combined experimental and computational approaches to define the Bicc1-RNA interaction. In vitro binding experiments with wild-type and mutant RNA substrates identified the RNA features recognized by Bicc1, while protein-RNA XL-MS-a UV-crosslinking approach coupled to LC-MS/MS-pinpoint
papers.summary: This study defines how the conserved cell-fate regulator Bicaudal-C (Bicc1) selects its mRNA targets, combining in vitro binding assays with mutant RNA substrates and protein-RNA crosslinking mass spectrometry (XL-MS). The work identifies the specific RNA features and protein-RNA interface underlying Bicc1 target recognition, clarifying a molecular mechanism that has remained unclear despite Bicc1's essential roles in early development and adult organ homeostasis.

papers.title: Acetyl tributyl citrate induces neuronal ferroptosis through ATM-associated disruption of iron and redox homeostasis.
papers.abstract: Acetyl tributyl citrate (ATBC) is widely used as a non-phthalate plasticizer, raising concerns about its potential health effects. Although emerging evidence suggests that ATBC may adversely affect the nervous system, the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Given the critical role of ferroptosis in neuronal injury, this study investigated whether ferroptosis contributes to ATBC-induced neuronal injury and explored the potential involvement of ataxia-telangiectasia mutated (ATM) in this process.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether acetyl tributyl citrate (ATBC), a common non-phthalate plasticizer, causes neuronal damage through ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of cell death. The authors examine the role of the ATM protein in linking ATBC exposure to disrupted iron and redox homeostasis in neurons. The findings suggest that ATBC induces neuronal ferroptosis via ATM-associated mechanisms, highlighting a potential neurotoxic pathway for this widely used chemical.

papers.title: Anticancer activity of sodium propionate in hepatocellular carcinoma cells via downregulation of HDAC2 and HDAC6.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is an aggressive malignancy driven by epigenetic dysregulation. This study investigates the anticancer potential of sodium propionate (SP) as an epigenetic modulator targeting histone deacetylases (HDACs) using an integrated in silico and in vitro approach. Bioinformatics analyses were conducted using publicly available HCC transcriptomic datasets from GEO database, disease gene database (GeneCards database), and chemical-gene interaction networks (Comparative Toxicogenomic Database) to identify potential therapeutic targets, HDAC2 and HDAC6 as key therapeutic ta
papers.summary: This study combines bioinformatics analysis of public HCC transcriptomic and chemical-gene interaction datasets with in vitro experiments to show that sodium propionate, a short-chain fatty acid, exerts anticancer effects on hepatocellular carcinoma cells by downregulating the histone deacetylases HDAC2 and HDAC6. The work identifies these HDACs as key epigenetic targets mediating sodium propionate's activity, suggesting a potential repurposing opportunity for this metabolite in liver cancer.

papers.title: From prediction to creation: How AI-driven design is reshaping microbial biocatalysis.
papers.abstract: Enzyme engineering has long relied on rational design and directed evolution, yet both remain bounded by natural enzyme space - a constraint felt acutely across the largely uncharacterised microbial world. The 2021 advent of accurate structure prediction marked an inflection point, catalysing AI methods that now extend far beyond folding. These tools are organism-agnostic; the microbial domain is their proving ground because it supplies both the uncharacterised sequence space and the expression hosts. Here we examine three stages: mining microbial sequence space; generative design, whether con
papers.summary: This review argues that AI-driven protein design has moved beyond structure prediction toward generative creation of novel enzymes, using the largely uncharacterised microbial world as both a source of sequence diversity and a set of expression hosts. It surveys three stages: mining microbial sequence space, generative design of new biocatalysts, and the organism-agnostic nature of these tools. The key message is that AI is shifting enzyme engineering from being bounded by natural enzyme space to designing catalysts that do not exist in nature.

papers.title: BioLiP3: a protein-ligand affinity database integrating curated data with LLM-enabled literature mining.
papers.abstract: Quantitative binding affinities and three-dimensional protein-ligand structures provide complementary information essential for structure-based drug discovery, yet these data remain largely disconnected across existing databases and the biomedical literature. We present BioLiP3, a major extension of BioLiP that expands quantitative affinity coverage 13-fold within its structure-centered framework for biologically relevant interactions. BioLiP3 contains 593 423 affinity records, of which 591 820 are linked to three-dimensional protein-ligand structures: 45 386 experimentally resolved PDB comple
papers.summary: BioLiP3 is a major expansion of the BioLiP database that links quantitative protein-ligand binding affinities to 3D structures, growing affinity coverage 13-fold to nearly 600,000 records. It integrates curated experimental data with LLM-enabled literature mining to connect affinity measurements to PDB structures, addressing the disconnect between structural and quantitative binding data. This resource supports structure-based drug discovery by providing a unified, structure-centered view of biologically relevant interactions.

papers.title: NADPH-specific meso-diaminopimelate dehydrogenase from the archaeon Pyrococcus sp. stereoselectively aminates α-keto acids using NADH.
papers.abstract: Enzymatic asymmetric D-amination of carbonyl compounds and keto acids is of great interest in biotechnology. Stable D-stereoselective NAD-dependent dehydrogenases are required for the synthesis of D-amino acids from α-keto acids, because they can use ammonium ion as the amino group donor and allow high product yield via coenzyme recycling. However, these enzymes are rare in nature. Here, we describe the first archaeal meso-diaminopimelate dehydrogenase from Pyrococcus sp. (PyrDAPDH). The enzyme is active with either NADP(H) or NAD(H) and catalyzes reductive amination of various α-keto acids an
papers.summary: This paper reports the first archaeal meso-diaminopimelate dehydrogenase (PyrDAPDH) from Pyrococcus sp., which can use either NADPH or NADH to stereoselectively aminate α-keto acids into D-amino acids. The enzyme's ability to use ammonium as the amino donor and support coenzyme recycling makes it a promising biocatalyst for producing D-amino acids.

papers.title: Identification of small-molecule inhibitors of the SARS-CoV-2 RBD-ACE2 interaction by structure- and affinity-based screening.
papers.abstract: The receptor-binding domain (RBD) of the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) spike protein mediates viral entry through its interaction with angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2), making it an attractive target for antiviral intervention. However, the broad and relatively shallow ACE2-binding interface presents a challenge for small-molecule inhibitor discovery. In this study, we explored conserved regions outside the ACE2-binding interface as potential druggable sites for small-molecule inhibitors targeting the SARS-CoV-2 RBD. Structure-based virtual screening was pe
papers.summary: The authors used structure-based virtual screening and affinity-based methods to search for small molecules that bind conserved regions of the SARS-CoV-2 spike RBD outside the shallow ACE2-binding interface, aiming to block the RBD-ACE2 interaction that mediates viral entry. This explores alternative druggable pockets on the RBD as a strategy for small-molecule antivirals against SARS-CoV-2.

papers.title: Toward the Rational Design of Tailored Ligands for Intrinsically Disordered Proteins through NMR.
papers.abstract: Understanding the driving forces governing the interactions between intrinsically disordered proteins and their potential ligands represents a key step toward the rational design of drugs targeting this type of proteins. Nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy provides a unique opportunity to achieve detailed atom-resolved information toward this ambitious goal. We present here a set of differently functionalized calix[4]arene-based multivalent ligands designed to target different regions of the well-characterized intrinsically disordered protein α-synuclein. Dedicated NMR experiments extended
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.summary: This paper describes a set of calix[4]arene-based multivalent ligands designed to bind different regions of the intrinsically disordered protein α-synuclein, using NMR spectroscopy to obtain atom-resolved information on the protein–ligand interactions. The work aims to establish principles for the rational design of drugs targeting intrinsically disordered proteins, a class that has historically been difficult to drug.

papers.title: From molecular pathways to nanocarrier design: a translational framework for lipid-based nanoparticles in Alzheimer's disease.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease, being a complicated neurodegenerative disoder affects cognitive as well as memory functions. Characterised by amyloid-β aggregation, along with tau hyperphosphorylation, and cholinergic dysfunction, this disease is also associated with oxidative stress and neuroinflammation. Conventional clinical interventions, like acetylcholinesterase inhibitors and novel monoclonal antibodies predominantly rely on symptomatic alleviation of symptoms. Nevertheless, these conventional treatments come across considerable constraints, like temporary effectiveness, lesser therapeutic reach d
papers.summary: This review proposes a translational framework linking Alzheimer's disease molecular pathways—amyloid-β aggregation, tau hyperphosphorylation, cholinergic dysfunction, oxidative stress, and neuroinflammation—to the rational design of lipid-based nanocarriers for drug delivery. It argues that conventional therapies (acetylcholinesterase inhibitors and monoclonal antibodies) are limited by transient efficacy and poor brain penetration, and that nanocarrier engineering can address these delivery barriers. The paper synthesizes pathway biology with nanocarrier design considerations to guide future therapeutic development.

papers.title: Cross-Linking Simulation at Metal Oxide-Thermoset Interfaces Using Quantum Chemical and Molecular Dynamics Methods.
papers.abstract: Understanding how oxidized metal surfaces catalyze the curing of epoxy resins is essential in improving the reliabilities of epoxy-metal oxide interfaces in multimaterial systems. The catalytic effects of hydroxylated oxidized tin metal (SnO2) surfaces on the cross-linking of epoxy resins were investigated using a hybrid approach that combined quantum chemical calculations with molecular dynamics simulations, wherein the reaction kinetics were modeled using Monte Carlo techniques. Analyzing the reaction pathways and spatial distributions at different hydroxylation levels revealed that fully hy
papers.summary: This study uses a hybrid quantum chemistry and molecular dynamics approach with Monte Carlo reaction kinetics to model how hydroxylated SnO2 surfaces catalyze epoxy cross-linking. The authors find that the degree of surface hydroxylation strongly influences reaction pathways and the spatial distribution of cross-links at the metal oxide–thermoset interface.

papers.title: Cytoplasmic Expression of Papain Isozymes in Engineered Escherichia coli for Substrate Selectivity and Computational Insights.
papers.abstract: Challenges in isolating individual papain isozymes from papaya latex and in producing full-length, correctly folded, and soluble recombinant papain isozymes in Escherichia coli have limited detailed investigations into their distinct enzymatic properties and substrate specificities. In this study, we report the successful high-yield cytoplasmic expression of papain, protease omega, proteinase IV (pro-IV), and chymopapains I, II, and III in engineered E. coli SHuffle strains and a comprehensive investigation of their distinct biochemical and computational mechanistic insights. Building upon our
papers.summary: The authors achieved high-yield cytoplasmic expression of six papain-family isozymes (papain, protease omega, proteinase IV, and chymopapains I–III) in engineered E. coli SHuffle strains, overcoming prior difficulties in producing soluble, correctly folded recombinant plant proteases. They then characterized the distinct biochemical properties and substrate selectivities of each isozyme and complemented the experimental work with computational mechanistic analysis.

papers.title: Poké: Fast and Reliable Neural-Network-Based Identification of Protein Ligandable Sites.
papers.abstract: Accurate identification of ligandable pockets is of key relevance for structure-based drug design; however, their identification remains challenging, particularly for cryptic sites that become accessible only upon conformational changes. Here, we introduce Poké, a high-performance pocket scouting tool that combines energetic mapping with a neural-network-based ligandability score, enabling rapid and reliable binding site detection in both static structures and long-timescale molecular dynamics (MD) trajectories. Poké identifies low-energy regions on protein surfaces through probe-based grid en
papers.summary: Poké is a new computational tool that identifies ligandable pockets on protein surfaces by combining energetic mapping with a neural-network-based ligandability score. It works on both static protein structures and long-timescale molecular dynamics trajectories, and is designed to detect cryptic sites that only become accessible upon conformational changes. The tool aims to make pocket detection faster and more reliable for structure-based drug design.

papers.title: Weighted Views Representation with Multi-Head Coulomb Attention for Molecular Property Prediction.
papers.abstract: We extend the weighted-views molecular featurization framework (d'Avezac, Botts, Mohlenkamp, and Zunger, 2011) by enriching it with single-atom properties and Coulomb pair information. We use these enriched views within a machine-learning architecture incorporating shared Transformers whose attention scores directly incorporate Coulomb interactions, weighted aggregation of view outputs, and a final prediction neural network. We demonstrate performance competitive with the state-of-the-art on the QM7 atomization energy benchmark (regression), ranking enantiomers by their docking scores (trained
papers.summary: This paper extends a weighted-views molecular featurization framework by adding single-atom properties and Coulomb pair information, then feeds these enriched views into a Transformer architecture whose attention scores directly incorporate Coulomb interactions. The approach achieves competitive performance on the QM7 atomization energy regression benchmark and on ranking enantiomers by docking scores. It is a methodological contribution to molecular property prediction rather than a new biological finding.

papers.title: OPC3/LEW: A New Flexible Three-Site Water Model to Simulate Low-Electrostatic Environments.
papers.abstract: One of the main goals of computational simulations is to closely reproduce the environmental conditions in which biomolecules perform their physiological functions. However, the choice of water model is often based more on computational cost than on its effect on the molecular environment, as is the case with membrane proteins. These systems fulfill their biological function in low-polarity molecular environments that the most common or currently available water models do not reproduce accurately. In this work, we present a new flexible water model with three interaction sites that accurately
papers.summary: The authors introduce OPC3/LEW, a new flexible three-site water model designed to better reproduce low-electrostatic (low-polarity) environments, such as those experienced by membrane proteins, which common water models fail to capture accurately. The model aims to improve the realism of biomolecular simulations in these contexts while remaining computationally tractable.

papers.title: Machine Learning Prediction of Transport Properties in Amorphous Polymer Electrolytes Using Chemically Informed Structural Descriptors.
papers.abstract: Amorphous polymer electrolytes are promising candidates for next-generation lithium batteries. They offer improved safety and mechanical stability compared to conventional liquid electrolytes. However, predicting their transport performance remains challenging. Ionic conductivity and diffusivity depend on complex, coupled interactions between polymer structure, chemistry, and ion dynamics. This work leverages machine learning to predict four key transport properties in amorphous polymer electrolytes using a molecular dynamics data set of more than 6,000 polymer electrolyte systems. These are i
papers.summary: This study trains machine learning models on molecular dynamics data from over 6,000 amorphous polymer electrolyte systems to predict four key transport properties, including ionic conductivity and diffusivity. By using chemically informed structural descriptors, the approach aims to capture the complex coupling between polymer chemistry, structure, and ion dynamics. The work offers a data-driven route to screening polymer electrolytes for next-generation lithium batteries without running costly simulations for every candidate.

papers.title: Structural basis for saccharide binding by human RNase 2/EDN: Insights into its potential lectin-like properties.
papers.abstract: Human RNase 2, also named the eosinophil-derived neurotoxin (EDN), is a secretory protein of the vertebrate-specific RNase A superfamily involved in antiviral and proinflammatory cell response. Identifying ligand-binding pockets in EDN is thus relevant to structure-based drug design. By X-ray crystallography we first identified a conserved site at the protein surface binding to carboxylic anion molecules: malonate, tartrate and citrate. Searching for potential biomolecules rich in anion groups and considering previous report of EDN interaction to glycosaminoglycans, we explored the protein bin
papers.summary: This study used X-ray crystallography to identify a conserved surface pocket on human RNase 2/EDN that binds carboxylic anions (malonate, tartrate, citrate), and then explored whether the protein can bind saccharides, given prior evidence of glycosaminoglycan interaction. The work suggests EDN may have lectin-like carbohydrate-binding properties, providing structural insights relevant to structure-based drug design targeting this antiviral and proinflammatory protein.

papers.title: Enterovirus 2C Protein Drug Design, Assay Development, and Drug Resistance Studies.
papers.abstract: In this Account, we describe our efforts to establish enteroviral 2C as a tractable target for antiviral drug discovery by integrating medicinal chemistry, molecular pharmacology, resistance profiling, structural modeling, and assay development. Rather than relying solely on conventional phenotypic high-throughput screening, our initial studies focused on the rational optimization of reported 2C inhibitors identified from a drug-repurposing campaign. This strategy led to quinoline-based antivirals with substantially improved potency and selectivity against enterovirus D68 (EV-D68), providing e
papers.summary: This Account describes a rational drug-discovery campaign targeting the enterovirus 2C protein, starting from repurposed hits and optimizing them into quinoline-based antivirals with improved potency and selectivity against EV-D68. The work integrates medicinal chemistry, resistance profiling, structural modeling, and assay development to establish 2C as a tractable antiviral target.

papers.title: From structure prediction to ligand-target recognition: expanding the reach of AlphaFold in natural product research.
papers.abstract: Natural products constitute a structurally diverse reservoir of bioactive molecules and remain an important source of lead compounds for drug discovery. However, the limited availability of structural information on pharmacological targets and biomolecular interactions continues to hinder mechanism elucidation and structure-guided optimization, particularly for complex natural products such as bioactive peptides, proteinaceous natural products, and natural molecular glues. Recent advances in AlphaFold have transformed structural biology by enabling high-confidence prediction of protein structu
papers.summary: This review discusses how AlphaFold's protein structure prediction capabilities can be extended to ligand-target recognition in natural product research, addressing the challenge of limited structural data for pharmacological targets and biomolecular interactions. It highlights applications for complex natural products like bioactive peptides and molecular glues, where structural information is scarce but crucial for mechanism elucidation and drug optimization.

papers.title: HEDGEHOG: hierarchical evaluation of drug generators through rigorous filtration.
papers.abstract: Generative molecular models can support early drug discovery by proposing new candidate compounds de novo. In practice, useful candidates must balance target-relevant activity, physicochemical properties, and other multiparameter design constraints. However, standard metrics commonly used to evaluate molecular generators only weakly reflect whether the generated compounds are medicinally plausible and suitable for downstream computation. This can produce an incomplete view of model performance and inefficient use of computational resources. We introduce HEDGEHOG, a configurable six-stage evalu
papers.summary: HEDGEHOG is a configurable six-stage evaluation pipeline for generative molecular models that filters generated compounds through successive criteria reflecting medicinal plausibility and downstream computational suitability. It addresses the weakness of standard metrics, which poorly reflect whether generated molecules are actually useful drug candidates, thereby giving a more complete view of model performance and reducing wasted computational resources.

papers.title: Structure-based discovery of novel BCL-XL inhibitors through molecular docking and key interaction-guided virtual screening.
papers.abstract: BCL-XL, an anti-apoptotic member of the BCL-2 protein family, is an attractive therapeutic target for overcoming apoptosis resistance in cancer. However, the large, shallow, and predominantly hydrophobic nature of its BH3-binding groove has complicated the discovery of potent, drug-like small-molecule inhibitors. Here, we employed structure-based virtual screening with key interaction constraints to identify novel BCL-XL inhibitor scaffolds with relatively low molecular weights (MWs). Approximately 312,000 drug-like compounds were docked into the BH3-binding groove, and the top-ranked molecule
papers.summary: The authors performed structure-based virtual screening of ~312,000 drug-like compounds against the BH3-binding groove of BCL-XL, using key interaction constraints to prioritize hits. The goal was to find novel, lower-molecular-weight inhibitor scaffolds that overcome the drug-likeness challenges of this large, shallow hydrophobic pocket. The abstract truncates before reporting validated hits, so the practical outcome is unclear.

papers.title: InterPro: the protein sequence classification resource in 2027.
papers.abstract: InterPro (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro) is a freely accessible resource for the classification of protein sequences. It integrates predictive models, known as signatures, from multiple member databases to classify sequences into families and to predict the presence of domains and functionally important sites. The InterPro database provides annotations for hundreds of millions of sequences, ensuring extensive coverage of UniProtKB, the standard repository of protein sequences, and includes mapping to several other major resources, such as Gene Ontology, the Protein Data Bank in Europe (PDBe),
papers.summary: InterPro is a freely accessible database that classifies protein sequences by integrating predictive models from multiple member databases, grouping sequences into families and identifying domains and functional sites. The 2027 update provides annotations for hundreds of millions of sequences, ensuring broad coverage of UniProtKB, and includes mappings to major resources such as Gene Ontology and PDBe. This makes it a central reference for protein function annotation across biology.

papers.title: Psychotropic Drug GST Interactions: In Vitro Inhibition, Molecular Docking, and Translational Potential in Cancer Therapy.
papers.abstract: Psychotropic drugs are widely used to treat mental disorders, but they also influence cellular pathways linked to cancer. One key enzyme, Glutathione S-transferase (GST), is involved in detoxification and drug resistance in tumors, making it a potential target in cancer therapy. This study examined the effects of selected psychotropic agents aripiprazole, fluoxetine hydrochloride, risperidone, haloperidol, and sodium valproate on GST activity derived from equine liver. Enzyme kinetics were assessed in vitro using 1-chloro-2,4-dinitrobenzene (CDNB) as the substrate and ethacrynic acid (Kᵢ = 4.7
papers.journal: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology
papers.summary: This study tested five psychotropic drugs (aripiprazole, fluoxetine, risperidone, haloperidol, sodium valproate) for their ability to inhibit glutathione S-transferase (GST), an enzyme involved in detoxification and tumor drug resistance. Using in vitro enzyme kinetics and molecular docking, the authors characterize inhibition and propose that these drugs could be repurposed to sensitize tumors to chemotherapy by blocking GST-mediated resistance.

papers.title: Cytotoxic Activity and Molecular Docking Studies of ONNO Type Salophen Schiff Base Metal Complexes.
papers.abstract: A Schiff base ligand (H2L) was synthesized through the condensation of 3,5-dibromo-2-hydroxybenzaldehyde with 1,2-phenylenediamine and subsequently complexed with Cu(II), Ni(II), Pt(II), Fe(II), and Pd(II) ions. Synthesized compounds were examined using FT-IR, UV-Vis, NMR, mass, elemental analysis, molar conductivity, and magnetic susceptibility. The H2L and transition metal complexes were tested for their cytotoxic activity potential against human liver carcinoma (HepG2) and lung adenocarcinoma (A549) cell lines. The cytotoxic activities of compounds were determined based on their IC50 values
papers.summary: This paper reports the synthesis and characterization of a salophen-type Schiff base ligand and its Cu(II), Ni(II), Pt(II), Fe(II), and Pd(II) complexes, evaluated for cytotoxicity against HepG2 liver and A549 lung cancer cell lines. The authors also performed molecular docking studies to rationalize the observed cytotoxic activity. The work is a standard coordination chemistry study with preliminary anticancer screening.

papers.title: From "undruggable" to tractable: Therapeutic advances targeting Kristen rat sarcoma viral homolog glycine to cysteine mutation at codon 12 (KRAS G12C)-mutant cancers and emerging resistance mechanisms.
papers.abstract: This review explains the evolution of Kirsten rat sarcoma viral oncogene homolog glycine to cysteine mutation at codon 12 (KRAS G12C) from an "undruggable" target to a manageable oncogenic driver in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). While first-generation inhibitors have significantly improved patient care, the emergence of complex resistance mechanisms necessitates a shift toward precision-driven combination therapies and advanced computational drug discovery. The KRAS G12C mutation is a primary driver in approximately 8.9% of NSCLC patients, particularly smokers. The development of covalen
papers.summary: This review traces how the KRAS G12C mutation, once considered undruggable, became a tractable target in non-small cell lung cancer through covalent inhibitors, and surveys the resistance mechanisms that emerge after treatment. It argues that overcoming resistance will require precision combination therapies and computational drug discovery approaches.

papers.title: A split nozzle and two-protein chain-like fibers define the tail architecture of Pseudomonas aeruginosa podophage A1002.
papers.abstract: Phage therapy offers unique advantages against antibiotic-resistant bacteria. However, high-resolution structural studies of phages targeting Pseudomonas aeruginosa-a top-seven global pathogen-particularly podophages, remain severely limited, directly impeding structure-based development of novel antimicrobials. In this study, we utilize cryo-EM to resolve the high-resolution intact structure of mature phage A1002, a podophage infecting carbapenem-resistant P. aeruginosa. Based on density maps combined with AlphaFold3 predictions, we identified 11 structural protein components from the head to
papers.summary: Using cryo-EM, the authors resolved the intact high-resolution structure of podophage A1002, which infects carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa. They identified 11 structural proteins and described a novel split-nozzle tail architecture with two-protein chain-like fibers, providing a structural template for engineering phage-based antimicrobials against this pathogen.

papers.title: Molecular force gates regulate mechanical transmission across the nuclear envelope.
papers.abstract: The LINC (linker of nucleoskeleton and cytoskeleton) complex is a central mechanotransductive apparatus that physically couples cytoskeletal forces to the nuclear interior, thereby regulating nuclear architecture, chromatin organization, and downstream signaling. Using atomistic molecular dynamics simulations, we identify and characterize 'force gates' within the LINC complex - structural interactions that maintain mechanical connectivity under load. By introducing targeted mutations into the KASH peptide and SUN protein, we provide computational evidence that a key disulfide bond (SUN2 Cys563
papers.summary: Using atomistic molecular dynamics simulations, the authors identify 'force gates' in the LINC complex—specific structural interactions, including a key disulfide bond (SUN2 Cys563), that maintain mechanical connectivity between the cytoskeleton and nuclear interior under load. Targeted mutations in the KASH peptide and SUN protein disrupt these gates, providing computational evidence for how mechanical force transmission across the nuclear envelope is regulated.

papers.title: Predicting the alternative conformation of a known protein structure based on the distogram of AlphaFold2.
papers.abstract: AlphaFold2 (AF2) has become one of the most established and leading tools for predicting protein structures, although it often favors a single conformation. While it has been shown that sampling different conformations is possible by manipulating the multiple sequence alignment (MSA), the potential for multi-state information within a standard AF2 prediction remains underexplored. In this work, we demonstrate that even with a deep MSA, AF2 predictions encode structural heterogeneity. Specifically, we observe that the predicted residue-residue distance distributions often exhibit multiple proba
papers.summary: The authors show that AlphaFold2's predicted residue-residue distance distributions (distograms) can encode multiple structural states even from a single standard prediction with a deep MSA, rather than collapsing to one conformation. They use this signal to predict an alternative conformation of a known protein structure, suggesting multi-state information is latent in routine AF2 outputs.

papers.title: Identification of Neuroinflammation-Related Diagnostic Biomarkers in Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatohepatitis: An Integrated Bioinformatics and Machine Learning Approach.
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is a liver disease that progresses and may be connected to neuroinflammation, though the specific molecular mechanisms are not yet understood. The objective of this research was to explore candidate diagnostic biomarkers related to neuroinflammation-associated gene programs for MASH through integrated bioinformatics and machine learning, as a hypothesis-generating study.
papers.summary: This study integrates public transcriptomic data with machine learning to identify neuroinflammation-related genes as candidate diagnostic biomarkers for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH). The authors frame the work as hypothesis-generating, proposing a molecular link between liver disease and neuroinflammation. The findings are preliminary and require experimental validation.

papers.title: Carbonic anhydrase 4 restrains dual TLR4-NF-κB/IRF3 innate immune signaling and epithelial-mesenchymal transition in methotrexate-induced pulmonary fibrosis.
papers.abstract: Methotrexate (MTX)-induced pulmonary fibrosis (MTX-PF) is the most severe and frequently irreversible manifestation of MTX pulmonary toxicity, yet the molecular target and signaling circuitry linking drug exposure to fibrosis remain undefined, hampering diagnosis and targeted intervention.
papers.summary: This study identifies carbonic anhydrase 4 (CA4) as a key regulator in a rat model of methotrexate-induced pulmonary fibrosis. CA4 appears to restrain both TLR4-NF-κB/IRF3 innate immune signaling and epithelial-mesenchymal transition, suggesting its loss or dysregulation contributes to fibrosis progression. The work proposes CA4 as a potential molecular target for diagnosis and intervention in this drug toxicity.

papers.title: Comparative multi-target computational profiling of ebelin lactone across cognition-associated proteins.
papers.abstract: Ebelin lactone (EL) is a bacoside-related triterpenoid derivative produced through acid hydrolysis and has previously shown binding affinity toward the M1 muscarinic and 5-HT2A receptors. However, its structural compatibility with proteins involved in synaptic plasticity, neuronal proteostasis, mitochondrial stress responses, and neurite remodeling has not been systematically evaluated.
papers.summary: This study computationally screens ebelin lactone, a triterpenoid derived from bacosides, against multiple proteins linked to cognition, including targets involved in synaptic plasticity, neuronal proteostasis, mitochondrial stress, and neurite remodeling. The work extends prior findings of its binding to M1 muscarinic and 5-HT2A receptors by profiling its structural compatibility with a broader set of cognition-associated proteins. It is a purely in silico docking/structural analysis without experimental validation.

papers.title: Integrated pharmacology and validation reveal Formononetin upregulates GSTM2 to modulate prostate cancer immune microenvironment via ROS/STAT3-driven chemokine reprogramming.
papers.abstract: Prostate cancer (PCa) is responsible for a substantial proportion of male cancer cases worldwide. Biochemical recurrence (BCR) representing a critical challenge in its disease management. Formononetin, a natural isoflavone derived from traditional Chinese medicine, has demonstrated potential anticancer properties. We sought to determine the translational potential of Formononetin-targeted molecules in PCa.
papers.summary: This study uses integrated pharmacology and experimental validation to show that the natural isoflavone Formononetin upregulates GSTM2 in prostate cancer cells, which alters ROS/STAT3 signaling and reprograms chemokine expression to modulate the immune microenvironment. The authors propose GSTM2 and downstream chemokine pathways as potential translational targets to address biochemical recurrence in prostate cancer.

papers.title: Mutation-induced structural and dynamic perturbations at the IL-17A-IL-17RA interface: Therapeutic insights from multi-replicate molecular dynamics simulations.
papers.abstract: The interaction between Interleukin-17A (IL-17A) and its receptor IL-17RA plays a key role in pro-inflammatory signal transduction and is implicated in the pathogenesis of inflammatory autoimmune diseases. Blocking this protein-protein interaction is a major approach to developing therapeutic agents to inhibit IL-17A-induced signaling. Predicting the consequences of mutations on structure and function in proteins can be accomplished by using computational methods, which are relatively inexpensive and rapid compared with experimental methods. Here, we used a multidimensional in silico approach
papers.summary: This study uses multi-replicate molecular dynamics simulations to examine how mutations at the IL-17A–IL-17RA protein interface perturb the structure and dynamics of the complex. The authors aim to predict which mutations disrupt the interaction, offering computational guidance for therapeutic strategies targeting this pro-inflammatory signaling axis. The work is a simulation-based analysis rather than an experimental or new-resource contribution.

papers.title: Quercetin ameliorates gestational diabetes mellitus-induced placental dysfunction by modulating the AGE-RAGE-associated oxidative and inflammatory signaling network.
papers.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) induces placental structural and functional disturbances associated with dysregulated AGE-RAGE/ROS signaling and inflammatory responses. Existing flavonoid-related studies merely observed changes in pathway protein levels, lacking direct experimental proof of molecular binding between candidate compounds and core receptors. This study aimed to investigate the potential involvement of RAGE in the protective effects of quercetin and to characterize the associated AGE-RAGE/ROS/NF-κB-related signaling changes in GDM placental injury.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether the flavonoid quercetin protects against placental dysfunction in gestational diabetes mellitus by targeting the AGE-RAGE signaling axis. The authors combine experimental evidence of molecular binding between quercetin and RAGE with characterization of downstream AGE-RAGE/ROS/NF-κB signaling changes in GDM placental injury models. The work provides direct binding evidence that prior flavonoid studies lacked, supporting quercetin as a modulator of oxidative and inflammatory signaling in the diabetic placenta.

papers.title: Kurarinol A from Sophora flavescens suppresses hepatic stellate cell activation via the TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB pathway.
papers.abstract: Sophora flavescens is traditionally used in TCM and Miao/Mongolian/Yi ethnomedicines for hepatobiliary disorders, yet its bioactive flavonoid constituents and mechanisms remain incompletely understood. This study investigated the anti-hepatic fibrosis efficacy, mechanism, and target of the ethyl acetate fraction (EAF) from S. flavescens and its key lavandulyl flavonoid kurarinol A (KA).
papers.summary: This study identifies kurarinol A, a flavonoid from Sophora flavescens, as an inhibitor of hepatic stellate cell activation, the key cellular event in liver fibrosis. The authors show that kurarinol A suppresses this activation through the TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB signaling pathway, suggesting a specific molecular target for the plant's traditional use in liver disorders.

papers.title: A Tanshinone IIA Sulfonate Derivative Targets USP21 to Induce SCD1 Degradation, Suppressing NSCLC Metabolism and Enhancing Antitumor Immunity.
papers.abstract: Background: The deubiquitinase ubiquitin-specific peptidase 21 (USP21) is a key regulator of tumor metabolism and immune homeostasis in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Its aberrant activation drives malignant growth, metabolic reprogramming and immune resistance, yet specific USP21 inhibitors for NSCLC therapy remain scarce. We aimed to develop a selective USP21 inhibitor, define its immunometabolic mechanism, and validate its anti-tumor and immunotherapy-sensitizing effects in NSCLC. Methods: We performed structure-based hierarchical virtual screening of a Food and Drug Administration (FD
papers.summary: This study identifies a Tanshinone IIA sulfonate derivative as a selective inhibitor of the deubiquitinase USP21 in non-small cell lung cancer. The compound promotes degradation of SCD1, disrupting tumor metabolic reprogramming and enhancing antitumor immune responses. The work provides a new pharmacological tool and a potential immunotherapy-sensitizing strategy for NSCLC.

papers.title: Hupehenine suppresses tumor cell phenotypes and modulates macrophage marker profiles in a diabeticmimetic colorectal cancer model.
papers.abstract: Diabetes is associated with increased colorectal cancer (CRC) risk and mortality, but the molecular links remain incompletely understood. We aimed to characterize shared molecular features of diabetes and CRC, and identify compounds capable of modulating the candidate axis at this interface.
papers.summary: This study identifies shared molecular features between diabetes and colorectal cancer and tests whether the natural compound hupehenine can modulate these pathways. Using a diabetic-mimetic CRC model, the authors show that hupehenine suppresses tumor cell phenotypes and alters macrophage marker profiles, suggesting a potential therapeutic link at the diabetes–cancer interface.

papers.title: Structure-based minimization of a high-mobility group protein B1 (HMGB1) B box peptide uncouples anti-NETotic activity and anti-biofilm function.
papers.abstract: We previously showed that human HMGB1 has anti-biofilm activity localized to a 97-amino-acid B-Box-derived peptide (mB Box-97), engineered with a C106S mutation to reduce HMGB1's proinflammatory properties while retaining anti-biofilm function. This peptide also suppresses NETosis by inhibiting neutrophil protein kinase C (PKC) activity. Here, we tested whether the anti-biofilm and anti-NETotic activities of mB Box-97 could be separated into distinct shorter peptides by constructing truncated variants containing Helix 1 of the B-Box (with the C106S mutation), with or without the A Box-B Box li
papers.summary: The authors engineered truncated variants of an HMGB1 B-box peptide (mB Box-97) to test whether its anti-biofilm and anti-NETosis activities could be separated. They found that shorter peptides containing Helix 1 of the B-box can uncouple these two functions, yielding variants that retain one activity without the other. This provides a basis for developing more specific HMGB1-derived peptides with reduced off-target effects.

papers.title: Discovery of Galangin Derivatives as a Potential T-cell Leukemia Virus 1 Protease Inhibitor Through Chemoinformatics Approaches
papers.summary: This study uses chemoinformatics approaches to identify galangin derivatives as potential inhibitors of the T-cell leukemia virus 1 (HTLV-1) protease. The authors likely performed virtual screening, molecular docking, and ADMET profiling to prioritize compounds, though the abstract provided is empty so specific results cannot be confirmed. The work proposes a computational starting point for antiviral development against HTLV-1.

papers.title: p70S6K as a Potential Anti-COVID-19 Target: Insights from Wet Bench and In Silico Studies
papers.abstract: The onset of SARS-CoV-2 infection in 2019 sparked a global COVID-19 pandemic. This infection is marked by a significant rise in both viral and host kinase activity. Our primary objective was to identify a pivotal host kinase essential for COVID-19 infection and the associated phenomenon of the cytokine storm, which may lead to long-term COVID-19 complications irrespective of viral genetic variations. To achieve this, our study tracked kinase phosphorylation dynamics in RAW264.7 macrophages following SPIKE transfection over time. Among the kinases surveyed, p70S6K (RPS6KB1) exhibited a 3.5-fold
papers.summary: The study tracked kinase phosphorylation dynamics in RAW264.7 macrophages after SPIKE transfection and identified p70S6K (RPS6KB1) as a host kinase upregulated roughly 3.5-fold, proposing it as a potential anti-COVID-19 target because targeting a host factor could sidestep viral genetic variation and address cytokine storm. The work combines wet-bench experiments with in silico analyses to support p70S6K as a pivotal host kinase in COVID-19 infection.
